```{r}
#| include: false
library(haven)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

file <- "data/Case 31 Data_efcu_1_HM_cleaned.sav"
d <- read_sav(file)
services <- paste0("q", 13:26)
categorical <- c("q9", "q10r", "q11", "q12")
ratings <- c("q7r", "q8r", "q30", paste0("q", 31:34), "q37r")
direct <- c("q2", "q28", "q29")
stopifnot(nrow(d) == 128, ncol(d) == 37,
          all(c(services, categorical, ratings) %in% names(d)),
          !any(direct %in% tolower(names(d))))
for (item in c("q7", "q8", "q10", "q37")) {
  upper <- if (item == "q10") 5 else 6
  stopifnot(identical(as.numeric(d[[paste0(item, "r")]]),
                      upper - as.numeric(d[[item]])))
}
labels <- c(q7r = "Savings rates", q8r = "Borrowing rates",
            q30 = "Loan rates lower than elsewhere",
            q9 = "Statement frequency", q10r = "Statement accuracy",
            q11 = "Statements easy to understand",
            q12 = "Account information kept confidential",
            q31 = "Personnel confidentiality",
            q32 = "Prompt loan processing",
            q33 = "Services meet member needs",
            q34 = "Simple loan applications",
            q37r = "Overall operations")
service_names <- vapply(d[services], function(x) tools::toTitleCase(attr(x, "label")), "")
pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x)
pval <- function(x) ifelse(x < .001, "< .001", sprintf("%.3f", x))
freq <- function(item) {
  x <- d[[item]]
  codes <- attr(x, "labels")
  codes <- codes[!tolower(names(codes)) %in% c("no answer", "no opinion")]
  values <- as.numeric(x)
  stopifnot(all(is.na(values) | values %in% unname(codes)))
  counts <- as.integer(table(factor(values, levels = unname(codes))))
  stopifnot(sum(counts) == sum(!is.na(values)), sum(counts) > 0)
  data.frame(Item = item, Response = names(codes), Count = counts,
             Valid = sum(counts), Share = counts / sum(counts))
}
dist <- setNames(lapply(c(services, categorical, ratings), freq),
                 c(services, categorical, ratings))
aware <- vapply(dist[services], function(x) sum(x$Share[1:2]), 0)
used <- vapply(dist[services], function(x) x$Share[1], 0)
gap <- aware - used
ref_label <- setNames(vapply(ratings, function(i) {
  labs <- attr(d[[i]], "labels")
  names(labs)[labs == 3]
}, ""), ratings)
tests <- setNames(lapply(ratings, function(i) t.test(as.numeric(d[[i]]), mu = 3)),
                  ratings)
gof <- setNames(lapply(c(services, categorical), function(i) {
  chisq.test(dist[[i]]$Count)
}), c(services, categorical))
stopifnot(all(vapply(gof, function(x) min(x$expected) >= 5, TRUE)))

display_freq <- function(i) {
  x <- dist[[i]]
  data.frame(Response = x$Response, Count = x$Count, `Valid %` = pct(x$Share),
             check.names = FALSE)
}
service_table <- function(items) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(items, function(i) {
    x <- dist[[i]]
    values <- sprintf("%d (%s)", x$Count, pct(x$Share))
    data.frame(Service = service_names[[i]], `Valid n` = x$Valid[1],
               Used = values[1], `Aware, unused` = values[2],
               Unaware = values[3], `Total aware` = pct(aware[[i]]),
               check.names = FALSE)
  }))
}
service_plot <- function(items) {
  x <- do.call(rbind, dist[items])
  x$Service <- factor(service_names[x$Item], levels = rev(service_names[items]))
  x$Response <- factor(x$Response, levels = dist[[items[1]]]$Response)
  ggplot(x, aes(Share, Service, fill = Response)) +
    geom_col(position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE), width = .68) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), limits = c(0, 1.001),
                       breaks = seq(0, 1, .25)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#12677C", "#68B7BC", "#D8E0EA")) +
    labs(x = "Percent of valid responses", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
}
rating_plot <- function(i) {
  x <- dist[[i]]
  x$Response <- factor(x$Response, levels = x$Response)
  ggplot(x, aes(Response, Count)) +
    geom_col(fill = "#12677C", width = .63) +
    geom_text(aes(label = pct(Share)), vjust = -.4, size = 5) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .14))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Responses") + theme_minimal(base_size = 16)
}
rating_table <- function(items) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(items, function(i) {
    x <- as.numeric(d[[i]])
    t <- tests[[i]]
    data.frame(Item = paste(labels[[i]], paste0("(", i, ")")),
               n = sum(!is.na(x)), Mean = sprintf("%.2f", mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
               SD = sprintf("%.2f", sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
               Reference = paste("3 =", ref_label[[i]]),
               t = sprintf("%.2f", t$statistic), df = unname(t$parameter),
               p = pval(t$p.value))
  }))
}
gof_table <- function(items) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(items, function(i) {
    g <- gof[[i]]
    data.frame(Item = if (i %in% services) service_names[[i]] else labels[[i]],
               n = sum(g$observed), `χ²` = sprintf("%.2f", g$statistic),
               df = unname(g$parameter), p = pval(g$p.value), check.names = FALSE)
  }))
}
response_pct <- function(i, codes) pct(sum(dist[[i]]$Share[codes]))
mean_text <- function(i) sprintf("%.2f", tests[[i]]$estimate)
best <- function(x) names(x)[x == max(x)]
worst <- function(x) names(x)[x == min(x)]
service_insight <- function(ids, x) paste(
  sprintf("%s (%s)", service_names[ids], pct(x[ids])), collapse = ", ")

```

## Data and methods

- Employees Federal Credit Union member opinion survey. R reads the cleaned Module 10 SPSS export directly (`r nrow(d)` records).
- Percentages use each item's valid responses. “No opinion” and “No answer” follow the existing missing-value decisions.
- The analysis-table key determines test type. The questionnaire and saved SPSS labels determine category meaning.
- Two-sided one-sample t-tests use the labeled midpoint for interval-treated ratings. Goodness-of-fit tests compare substantive response shares with equal shares. The key gives the test type, and equal shares are the reference assumption used here.

## R1 · Reasons for joining

**Why do people join the Credit Union?**

Q2 allows multiple reasons per member, including convenience, savings rates, personal service, access to borrowing, advertising and Other. The extract lacks Q2, so the distribution of joining reasons is unavailable.

### Savings-rate perception (q7r)

```{r}
#| label: fig-savings
#| fig-cap: "Savings-rate ratings. Bar labels show valid-response percentages."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.2
rating_plot("q7r")
```

`r response_pct("q7r", 3)` of valid respondents rated savings rates **Average** (@fig-savings).

## R1 · One-sample t-test

```{r}
#| label: tbl-savings
#| tbl-cap: "Savings-rate rating versus Average."
kable(rating_table("q7r"))
```

The data provided insufficient evidence that the mean differed from **Average** (@tbl-savings). The scale runs from Very low to Very high. The item captures members’ assessment of savings rates.

## R2 · Reasons for borrowing elsewhere

**Why do members use other financial institutions when they need to borrow funds?**

- Q28 screens for borrowing elsewhere in the past year. A No response skips Q29. Q29 lists reasons such as better rates, an established credit line and preference for a local institution. Its wording leaves the number of permitted choices unspecified.
- Both fields are absent. The key supplies two contextual measures, **q8r** for perceived borrowing-rate level and **q30** for agreement that EFCU rates are lower than elsewhere.

## R2 · Rate perceptions

```{r}
#| label: fig-borrowing
#| fig-cap: "Perceived borrowing-rate level (q8r). Bar labels show valid-response percentages."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.5
rating_plot("q8r")
```

`r response_pct("q8r", 3)` rated borrowing rates **Average** (@fig-borrowing). For q30, `r response_pct("q30", 4:5)` agreed or strongly agreed that EFCU rates were lower than elsewhere.

## R2 · One-sample t-tests

```{r}
#| label: tbl-loan-rates
#| tbl-cap: "Loan-rate perceptions versus their scale references."
kable(rating_table(c("q8r", "q30")))
```

`r paste(vapply(c("q8r", "q30"), function(i) {
  t <- tests[[i]]
  direction <- if (t$estimate > 3) "above" else "below"
  if (t$p.value < .05) paste0(labels[[i]], " (", i, ") averaged significantly ", direction, " “", ref_label[[i]], ".”")
  else paste0("For ", i, ", evidence was insufficient to establish a difference from “", ref_label[[i]], ".”")
}, ""), collapse = " ")` See @tbl-loan-rates.

## R5 · Service awareness and use

**How well are the members aware of the services offered by the credit union?**

- Highest awareness: `r service_insight(best(aware), aware)`.
- Lowest awareness: `r service_insight(worst(aware), aware)`.
- Signature loans had the largest gap. Awareness was `r pct(aware[["q18"]])`, and reported use was `r pct(used[["q18"]])` (`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * gap[["q18"]])` percentage points).
- Each service has one response per member. Total awareness includes both aware categories.


## R5 · Goodness of fit

`r sum(vapply(gof[services], function(x) x$p.value < .05, TRUE))` of `r length(services)` services had response shares that differed from equal thirds at the item-level .05 threshold. The charts show which categories were most common.

```{r}
kable(gof_table(services[1:7]))
```

## R5 · Goodness of fit (continued)

```{r}
kable(gof_table(services[8:14]))
```

## R6 · Operational effectiveness

**What are the members’ attitudes and beliefs about how effectively the credit union is operated?**

- `r response_pct("q9", 3)` said statements came **About Right**.
- `r response_pct("q10r", 3:4)` rated statement accuracy **Good** or **Excellent**. Higher q10r scores indicate better perceived accuracy.
- `r response_pct("q11", 1)` found statements easy to understand, and `r response_pct("q12", 1)` said account information was kept confidential.

## R6 · Goodness of fit

```{r}
#| label: tbl-operations-gof
#| tbl-cap: "Response distributions versus equal category shares."
kable(gof_table(categorical))
```

The test uses every substantive questionnaire category, including categories with zero responses. The reference is equal shares across five q9 categories, four q10r categories, or two Yes/No categories. See @tbl-operations-gof.

## R6 · Operations and overall management

```{r}
#| label: tbl-operations-ratings
#| tbl-cap: "Item-level ratings and two-sided one-sample tests."
kable(rating_table(ratings[4:8]))
```

Higher q31–q34 ratings indicate stronger agreement. Higher q37r indicates a more favorable overall management and operations rating.

All five means were above their respective scale references (each `r paste0("p ", pval(max(vapply(tests[ratings[4:8]], function(x) x$p.value, 0))))`).

## R6 · What respondents reported

- `r response_pct("q31", 4:5)` agreed or strongly agreed that personnel keep personal financial information confidential.
- `r response_pct("q32", 4:5)` agreed or strongly agreed loan applications are processed promptly.
- `r response_pct("q33", 4:5)` agreed or strongly agreed that services meet members’ needs.
- `r response_pct("q34", 4:5)` agreed or strongly agreed that applications are simple to complete.
- `r response_pct("q37r", 4:5)` rated overall operations **Good** or **Excellent**. See @tbl-operations-ratings for comparisons with the scale reference.

## Overall findings

- **R1.** The most common savings-rate rating was **Average**. Joining reasons require Q2.
- **R2.** The rate items describe members’ perceptions of EFCU’s lending rates. The reasons for borrowing elsewhere require Q28 and Q29.
- **R5.** Awareness and use varied by service. The largest gap was for `r paste(service_names[best(gap)], collapse = ", ")`.
- **R6.** Statement accuracy was generally rated favorably, and the overall management and operations rating averaged `r mean_text("q37r")` on a five-point scale.

## Limitations

- Q2, Q28 and Q29 are absent from the Module 10 extract. The analysis follows the key’s rate measures while keeping the direct reasons unresolved.
- The narrative describes 125 returns and two exclusions. The supplied extract has `r nrow(d)` records, and the case materials do not explain that difference.
- Results describe reported views and use. The q30–q34 items measure separate perceptions. Test p-values are unadjusted and interpreted per item.
